page: Amazon Web Services m5.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8175M processor with an x86_64 architecture, providing 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz and includes 33 MB of L3 cache, alongside support for Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX) and AVX-512F. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks position the m5.4xlarge primarily in the average tier for multi-core and memory operations. While single-core performance, such as stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores, falls into the lower 25% tier, multi-core execution scales to average levels. Memory bandwidth tests, including uncached read and write operations, consistently register average speeds. Cryptographic and database operations, such as Redis SET operations and Passmark database tests, also perform within the middle 50% benchmark range. However, single-threaded compression and decompression tasks show weaker performance.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m5.4xlarge offers a balanced resource density suitable for general-purpose workloads that do not require specialized local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. The 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it a stable choice for standard enterprise applications. It is well-suited for workloads such as static web serving, software compilation, medium-scale database operations, and general-purpose application hosting.
